comment: Read from the maker's source and README at commit e6aebea, the head of main and the only commit carrying the installed 2.0.1. Panel names were read from a render of res/sequence_enhancer.svg: ALG., PITCH, RYTM., SPD., GATE, CLK, RST, IN, OUT. Several are printed twice — SPD. and GATE each label a slider, a trimpot and a CV jack, and GATE also labels the gate input and the gate output — and the labels are set below their group rather than beside each control, so no line leads with one. Index order is not panel order. The parameters run Algorithm, Pitch Amount, Speed slider, Gate Length slider, Rhythm Amount, Speed trimpot, Gate trimpot, so index 4 is the lowest knob on the right while indexes 5 and 6 are the two trimpots further up on the left. The inputs are worse: index 5 is the pitch input in the second row from the bottom, while indexes 6, 7 and 8 are CLK, RST and GATE along the bottom row, and indexes 0 to 4 are the five CV jacks scattered up the panel. Three conflicts with the maker's own text. The README lists the speed slider as 1/4x, 1/2x, 3/4x, 1x, 2x, 3x, 4x; the code's clockMult table in sequence_enhancer_channel.hpp updateSpeed gives 4, 3, 2, 1, 0.75, 0.5 and 0.25 clocks per step, which is a quarter, a third, a half, the same, four thirds, twice and four times the clock. The maker's own switch labels in configSwitch agree with the code except at the fifth position, which they print as 1.5x where the table gives four thirds; the line follows the table. The README also says all CV inputs can be attenuated where only speed and gate length have a trimpot. The algorithm CV is declared as setAlg(int param, int cv) and called with a float voltage, so the voltage is truncated to whole volts before the 0.7 scaling; this is very likely not what was meant, but it is what the installed build does. There is no context menu and no lights, so there are no menu lines.
